newsitem.title: GERMANY: Christmas shopping off to poor start in Germany.
newsitem.headline: Christmas shopping off to poor start in Germany.

text.p: German retailers said the Christmas shopping season has gotten off to a poorer start than last year.
Shoppers' spirits were dampened by wet weather on the first Saturday of Advent, the traditional start to the biggest shopping season of the year, said the Association of German Retailers (HDE).
A survey of 60 retailers showed none whose sales exceeded last year's, and only a few where they were roughly equal. The number of customers was high, but they bought less.

Still, prominent establishments such as the KaDeWe department store in Berlin, Europe's largest, and Oberhausen's CentrO, the largest mall in continental Europe, said they were satisfied with the day's receipts.
HDE said sales in November and December this year were expected to total 26 billion marks, two billion marks more than last year.
Longer weekday store opening hours could mean more consumers plan to do their shopping then, rather than on Saturdays, HDE said.
The weather in Dresden was dry but cold, and an official at the Hertie department store said the season was off to a cautious start.
The head of Munich's Karstadt department store said, "We are not satisfied so far."
